title: Save and reload a quad layout without recomputation
description:
Persist a finished layout so scenes can load it instantly (Quad Layouts note: 'need to solve for loading arb quad layout so we can have quick iteration' and 'store all of the quad layout information ... into files for caching'). There is no serializer today: QuadLayoutEngine produces an ArcNetwork (nodes/arcs/patches, id == index, retired via alive flags) and PatchSurfaceGeometry bundles with the per-face patch_id IntField. Per the standing one-language ruling, the saved form is a .dsl graph: `load_mesh` of the source file followed by network_node / network_arc / network_patch / arc_network statements with geometric anchors (node = nearest_vertex position, arc = shortest edge path with via-waypoints, patch = four corner nodes + side counts), exactly the form of src/main/resources/dsl/fixtures/*.dsl, emitted by a new QuadLayoutDslWriter (sorted, byte-stable). Add a `save-layout <path>` terminal command and a `--property quadLayout.save=<path>` for headless runs; ModelCatalog lists saved layouts as ModelChoice.Kind.DSL so the model menu and -Dixdar.model can pick them. Loading is the existing graph path (registerGraph/GraphChoice), so no new reader is needed if the writer's output re-traces exactly. Related: PATCH-57 (emit Coons-patch DSL from T-mesh patches, pinned) covers the Coons-surface half of a saved layout; this ticket covers the arc network itself.

SCOPE CORRECTION (user, 2026-09-05): the first pass saved the embedded/contracted T-mesh from the embedded-tmesh scene. That is not the deliverable. The deliverable is the QUAD LAYOUT OUTPUT of the quad-layout scene after the full pipeline: the final conforming layout (engine.tmesh, 284 patches on fertility) together with the extracted quad mesh (engine.quadBundle, 13853 quads) and the patch surfaces carrying patch_id (engine.patchSurfaces / patchCoons). Constraint discovered: GridMapAssembly needs the seamless parametrization (engine.seamless), so the quad mesh cannot be regenerated from a saved network without re-running the solver stages. Therefore the saved .dsl must persist results, not inputs: use the extracted quad mesh itself as the carrier (OffMeshWriter can write quads), emit the layout nodes/arcs/patches geometrically ON THAT QUAD MESH (layout arcs are chains of quad-mesh edges, so shortest-edge-path re-tracing with via waypoints reproduces them exactly), and let arc_network/network_patch derive each patch's face set so a per-face patch_id can be rebuilt on load. The pre-refinement T-mesh save from embedded-tmesh may stay as a secondary feature but the quad-layout scene's save-layout is what must work.
definition-of-done:
1. `save-layout` on the plane and torus fixtures writes a .dsl that, re-executed, yields an ArcNetwork element-equal to the original (same node positions, arc paths, patch corners). 2. `save-layout` on fertility (284 patches) writes a .dsl that reloads in EmbeddedTMeshScene with identical patch count and boundaries. 3. Saved layouts appear in the model menu and can be launched with -Dixdar.model=<saved.dsl>. 4. Writer output is byte-stable across two runs (TreeMap/sorted emission). 5. Round-trip unit test lives in test/unit/mesh using the plane/torus fixtures only. 6. Build checkstyle-green.

7. save-layout in the quad-layout scene after the full pipeline writes a .dsl whose carrier is the extracted quad mesh; re-executing it yields 13853 quad faces, 284 patches, and a per-face patch_id partition identical to engine.patchSurfaces (same face sets per patch), with NO cross-field, seamless, motorcycle, quantization, embedding, grid-map or Newton stage run. 8. The quad-layout scene reloads that file (model menu / -Dixdar.model) and renders patch fill (P), boundaries (B) and the quad grid (Q) identically to the live run; the CRAW-4 launch.json entry targets the quad-layout scene with the saved quad-layout output, not embedded-tmesh.
testing-plan: 1. QuadLayoutDslWriterTest: save torus_layout fixture -> execute -> compare ArcNetwork element-exact. 2. Benchmark (test/benchmark) saving/reloading fertility; assert patch count 284 and boundary arc count. 3. run-scene embedded-tmesh with the saved fertility .dsl, screenshot, compare with a live-computed run. 4. Diff two consecutive saves of the same layout to prove byte stability.

unknowns: Whether shortest-edge-path re-tracing reproduces every arc exactly on dense meshes with near-tie paths; if not, the fallback is a sidecar in the CrossFieldWriter pattern -- requires a user ruling because of the one-language rule
Whether the saved graph should also carry the quantized arc lengths (network_arc length=) so quantization is skipped on reload
How to reference the source mesh path portably (relative to IXDAR_MODEL_DIR?)

Via budget ceiling: fertility needs 1449 via waypoints over 568 arcs, worst arc 30, so NetworkArc.VIA_COUNT was raised 8 to 32 -- only 2 of margin, and the crawfish scans are ~45x denser. The fixed via1..viaN port form is forced by the DSL having no list literal and PortType no list-of-vector type. Options: raise the cap again per mesh; add a VECTOR3_LIST port type plus a DSL list literal and emit path=[...] (clean, but touches lexer/parser and the node ABI); or split over-budget arcs into node chains (rejected, not element-exact). Needs a ruling.

QuadLayoutScene's post-pipeline T-mesh cannot be saved: the extraction/grid-map stages refine the working copy further after recarve (copy V=15003 -> 19219) without updating the T-mesh's stored arc paths, so a stored consecutive vertex pair is no longer an edge of the current copy and the writer throws ('arc 435 steps from copy vertex 14130 to 3819 along an edge that is not the unique shortest path'). The fertility artifact is saved from embedded-tmesh after C instead. Whether the later stages should keep the T-mesh paths in step is a pipeline question outside this ticket.

Saved layouts live in ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/layouts, which puts the 896K carrier .off into target/classes and any shipped jar. If that is unwanted, ModelCatalog.LAYOUT_DIR is the single place to change.

Whether the Coons variant (patchCoons) must also be persisted or can be rebuilt from the per-patch grids of the reloaded quad mesh (PatchGridExtraction from a quad partition rather than from GlobalGridMap)

Whether the pre-refinement T-mesh (topology on the triangle working copy) is needed downstream at all once the quad-level layout is saved; if yes it needs the carrier to be the refined working copy with arcs remapped onto it

Patch NUMBERING on reload is the writer's geometric order, not the pipeline's internal patch ids, so PatchColorHash paints the reloaded layout in a different palette even though the face partition is identical. Preserving the pipeline's ids means writing a literal id (against the one-language ruling); the alternative is colouring by a geometric key (e.g. the first corner node's position), which would change the live scene too. Needs a ruling.

The saved layout carries no Coons variant: the reloaded bundle is a flat face partition with no per-patch row/column structure, so the quad-layout scene's C (Coons fill) toggle does nothing on a reloaded layout. Recovering each patch's grid shape by walking its component's quad strips is the follow-on.

quadLayout.save fires at model load, which is correct for quad-layout (loadModel runs the pipeline) but wrong for embedded-tmesh, where the layout only reaches 284 patches after the C keypress -- saving there at load writes the uncontracted T-mesh and fails the via budget (arc 33 needs 47). That scene needs the save-layout terminal command after C.
changes-made: QuadLayoutDslWriter (nodes/network) serializes a live ArcNetwork as an authored .dsl: carrier statement, arc_network, then every live node (nearest-vertex position, critical/border flags), arc (unique-shortest-edge-path legs between the fewest via waypoints, quantized length, feature flag) and patch (four corner nodes plus four side arc counts). Sorted by geometry, never by id, so output is byte-stable across JVMs.

OffMeshWriter writes a triangle HalfEdgeMesh back to ASCII OFF, for the carrier mesh a pipeline layout needs: 229 of 278 fertility nodes and 556 of 568 arcs sit on vertices the refinement minted, so the source _in_tri.off cannot carry the network.

save-layout / sl <path.dsl> terminal command plus the quadLayout.save system property; ModelScene gained layoutNetwork(), saveLayout() and a render-thread pendingSavePath queue, with EmbeddedTMeshScene and QuadLayoutScene overriding layoutNetwork().

ModelCatalog scans src/main/resources/dsl/layouts and lists each saved layout as ModelChoice.Kind.DSL named '<stem> (layout)'; ModelScene.loadModelOrGraph dispatches a .dsl path to loadGraph, and NodeGraphRuntime retries a relative graph path under the ixdar-app module directory as mesh paths already do.
NetworkArc.VIA_COUNT raised 8 to 32: fertility's worst arc needs 30 via waypoints and 24 of 568 arcs exceeded the old budget of 8. No sidecar format was added.

Dijkstra gained a stopVertex bound and UniqueShortestPath a forestFrom/find(forest) split. Re-tracing ran one full 15003-vertex distance field per arc leg, making reload (6.9s) slower than recompute (5.7s); stopping once the target is settled is semantically identical and took reload to 0.6s against a 4.3s recompute.

Checked in the saved 284-patch fertility layout (ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/layouts/fertility_layout.dsl, 154147 bytes, plus its 15003-vertex carrier .off), produced through the real save-layout command after contracting in embedded-tmesh, and a 'CRAW-4: Embedded T-Mesh (saved fertility layout)' launch.json entry verified to reach 284 patches with no pipeline run.

Verified: 161 tests with only the known DenseMeshFewSplitsTest baseline failure; round trip element-exact on the plane and torus fixtures; fertility reload 278 nodes / 568 arcs / 284 patches; the layout saved in one JVM, reloaded in another and re-saved there produced zero differing network statements and a byte-identical carrier. Details in the worktree's VERIFICATION.md.

SCOPE CORRECTION PASS: the saved artifact is now the quad-layout scene's output. QuadCarrierLayout restates the finished layout on the extracted quad mesh (grids.quadVertexByNodeId for nodes, grids.chainByArc for arcs, the same side chains for patches), so the carrier .off IS the pipeline's 13853-quad result and the .dsl only re-attaches the layout to it. GridMapAssembly needs engine.seamless, so results are persisted, never inputs.

quad_layout_surfaces (new mesh node) closes every saved graph: LayoutPatchPartition floods the carrier's faces from the arc walls, seeded from each arc's left/right flank (interior left of walk), and PatchSurfaceGeometry.partitionBundle emits them one component per patch with the patch_id per-face IntField -- the same bundle shape engine.patchSurfaces has, so QuadLayoutRuntime renders P/B/Q from it unchanged. The node also passes net through, so lastOutput('net') still works.

EmbeddedMeshTopology accepts a uniform non-triangle carrier (reads the source's own face arity, refuses mixed arity, bulkAllocate for quads, barycentrics registered only for triangles); OffMeshWriter writes n-gon faces and takes a MeshTopology, so the quad carrier round-trips as 13853 quads through OffMeshParser's existing uniform-quad path; QuadLayoutRuntime.setCopyWireframe walks each face's real corner count.

Fertility, full pipeline then save then reload from the .dsl alone: 13853 quads, 284 patches, euler -6, singularities 44, 278 nodes / 568 arcs, reload 0.4s against a 6.9s pipeline (headless scene ready in 2.1s vs 10.1s, with no stage line in the log). The reloaded per-face patch_id partition is EQUAL FACE-SET FOR FACE-SET to engine.patchSurfaces (compared by sorted corner positions, numbering-free).

Via waypoints collapse on the quad carrier: 2 in total across 568 arcs, worst arc 1, against 1449 / worst 30 on the triangle working copy. A layout arc is a chain of quad-mesh edges and a straight run along a grid line is the unique shortest path, so VIA_COUNT=32 is no longer near its ceiling on this path.

Checked in ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/layouts/fertility_quad_layout.dsl (102021 bytes, 1134 lines) plus its 13847-vertex / 13853-quad carrier .off, written by the real command (--property quadLayout.save on the quad-layout scene). Byte-stable across three JVMs: 0 differing lines after the carrier line, carrier byte-identical. Removed the first pass's misleading pre-extraction fertility_layout.dsl/_carrier.off.

Fixed the web build, which the first pass had silently broken: TeaVM has no Arrays.compare, so classes.js was 36 bytes on a zero exit. QuadLayoutDslWriter now uses hand-written lexicographic row comparators; classes.js is back to 6797513 bytes and the saved artifact is byte-identical before and after the swap.

launch.json: 'CRAW-4: Embedded T-Mesh (saved fertility layout)' replaced by 'CRAW-4: Quad Layout (saved fertility quad layout)' -- scene quad-layout, -Dixdar.model=src/main/resources/dsl/layouts/fertility_quad_layout.dsl, cwd ${workspaceFolder}/ixdar-app, verified by running those exact vmArgs from that cwd.

163 tests, 1 failure (the known DenseMeshFewSplitsTest baseline), 1 skipped; checkstyle green. New unit fixture dsl/fixtures/plane_quad_layout.dsl (quad mesh_grid, no mesh file) round-trips element-exact and partitions its carrier 8/8/16 over 32 quads.
